authoredSolutions.51: For \(\sin^{-1}\): \(-1\le 2x^2-3x+1\le 1\Rightarrow 2x^2-3x\le 0\Rightarrow 0\le x\le \tfrac32\). For \(\cos^{-1}\): on \([0,\tfrac32]\), \(11-3x>0\) and \(-1\le\frac{2x-5}{11-3x}\le 1\) holds throughout. Hence the domain is \([0,\tfrac32]\), so \(\alpha=0,\ \beta=\tfrac32\) and \(\alpha+2\beta=3\).
authoredSolutions.52: The ellipse \(x^2+4y^2=4\) has \(a=2,\ b=1\), area \(\pi ab=2\pi\). The curves \(y=|x|-1\) and \(y=1-|x|\) bound a square with vertices \((\pm1,0),(0,\pm1)\), area \(\tfrac12\cdot2\cdot2=2\), lying inside the ellipse. Required area \(=2\pi-2=2(\pi-1)\).
authoredSolutions.53: Reflexivity forces all \(4\) diagonal pairs to be present. Symmetry means each of the \(\binom{4}{2}=6\) unordered off-diagonal pairs is independently included or not. Hence the count is \(2^{6}=64\).

authoredSolutions.71: Equal roots require discriminant \(0\): \(4f'^2-4f f''=0\Rightarrow f'^2=f f''\), whose solution is \(f(x)=e^{kx}\). From \(f(0)=1,\ f'(0)=2\) we get \(f(x)=e^{2x}\), which is increasing. So \(f(\ln x-x)\) increases where \(\frac{d}{dx}(\ln x-x)=\frac1x-1>0\Rightarrow 0<x<1\). Thus \((\alpha,\beta)=(0,1)\) and \(\alpha+\beta=1\).
authoredSolutions.72: The added term equals \(\frac{2}{(n+1)^2}-\frac{1}{n^2}\). Setting \(c_n=a_n-\frac{2}{n^2}\) gives \(c_{n+1}=\frac12 c_n\) with \(c_1=a_1-2=-1\), so \(c_n=-(1/2)^{n-1}\). Then \(\sum_{n\ge1}c_n=-\frac{1}{1-1/2}=-2\), whose absolute value is \(2\).

authoredSolutions.74: By Cayley-Hamilton \(A^2=4A-2I\Rightarrow A^3=14A-8I=\begin{bmatrix}20&28\\14&20\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B^2=3B-I\Rightarrow B^3=8B-3I=\begin{bmatrix}5&8\\8&13\end{bmatrix}\). Then \(A^3-B^3=\begin{bmatrix}15&20\\6&7\end{bmatrix}\) with \(\det=-15\). For a \(2\times2\) matrix \(\det(\operatorname{adj}M)=\det M\), so the value is \((-15)^2=225\).
authoredSolutions.75: \(\sin3x+\sin2x+\sin x=\sin2x(2\cos x+1)=2\sin x\cos x(2\cos x+1)\), vanishing at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{2\pi}{3}\).
